welcome_lead: Today you'll trace the thaw of détente and the collapse of the Soviet bloc.

concepts.def: 1968 reform under Dubček, crushed in August
1968 — USSR could invade any socialist state
Easing of tensions in the 1970s — SALT I in 1972
Soviet leader from 1985 — glasnost and perestroika
9 November 1989 — end of the Iron Curtain

walkthroughs.body_html:
Alexander Dubček promised 'socialism with a human face' in Czechoslovakia.

On 20-21 August 1968 Warsaw Pact tanks invaded. Brezhnev announced the Brezhnev Doctrine: no socialist country could leave the bloc.

The 1970s brought détente: SALT I (1972), the Helsinki Accords (1975) and Apollo-Soyuz.

It froze again in 1979 when the USSR invaded Afghanistan. Reagan called the USSR an evil empire and launched 'Star Wars' (SDI) in 1983.

From 1985, Gorbachev launched glasnost (openness) and perestroika (restructuring).

He scrapped the Brezhnev Doctrine. In 1989 Solidarity won Polish elections, the Berlin Wall fell on 9 November, and Eastern Europe broke free. The USSR dissolved on 26 December 1991.
